steps.body: A diagram makes the plan visible: equal parts for the groups, a crossed-off piece for what comes away, and a label for the unit.
steps.narration: A diagram makes the plan visible: equal parts for the groups, a crossed-off piece for what comes away, and a label for the unit.

widget.prompt: Draw the diagram for 6 laps of 400 m: build six equal parts, in hundreds of meters.
widget.successFeedback: Six equal parts of four hundred meters — 2,400 m before the 150 m shortfall comes off the end.
widget.partialFeedback: Every lap is the same length: build each bar to four hundreds of meters.

predict.prompt: 150 m crossed off the END of the bar means…
predict.reveal: A mark at the end of the whole bar removes 150 m one time; a mark inside every part would remove it six times.

cml.actionGoal: Read where an adjustment sits in a bar diagram and translate that placement into an expression.
invariants: A mark at the end adjusts the total once; a mark inside every part adjusts each group.
misconceptions: Treating an end adjustment as though it occurred inside every group.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the unit got ten times smaller, what would happen to the number that measures the same object?

widget.prompt: A bar diagram shows 6 equal parts of 400 m, with 150 m crossed off the end. What does it record?

options.label: (6 × 400) − 150 = 2,250 m
options.feedback: Correct — six equal laps build 2,400 m, and the crossing-off removes 150 from the whole bar once.

options.label: 6 × (400 − 150) = 1,500 m
options.feedback: That shortens EVERY lap by 150; the diagram crosses off 150 once, at the end.

options.label: 6 + 400 − 150 = 256 m
options.feedback: Equal parts stack into a product, not a sum — six parts of 400 is 6 × 400.

options.label: (6 × 400) + 150 = 2,550 m
options.feedback: Crossed off means removed, so the final step subtracts.

widget.successFeedback: Four equal parts of three hundred meters show 1,200 meters before any adjustment.
widget.partialFeedback: Each lap has the same length; build every bar to three hundreds of meters.

widget.prompt: Apply without the opening model: A hiker walks 7 laps of 200 meters and stops 123 meters early. How many meters?

commonErrors.feedback: That reported the full distance; the hiker stopped 123 meters before finishing.
Stopping early SHORTENS the walk, so the last step subtracts.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Multiply to build the equal-group total, then subtract the one stated adjustment.

widget.prompt: Diagnose a second diagram: four 300-meter parts each have 50 meters crossed off inside the part. What does it record?

options.label: 4 × (300 − 50) = 1,000 meters
options.feedback: Correct — the crossing occurs inside every part, so each of the four laps is shortened.

options.label: (4 × 300) − 50 = 1,150 meters
options.feedback: That subtracts 50 only once, as if the mark sat at the end of the whole bar.

options.label: 4 + 300 − 50 = 254 meters
options.feedback: Four equal 300-meter parts combine by multiplication, not by adding unlike quantities.

options.label: 4 × (300 + 50) = 1,400 meters
options.feedback: Crossed off means removed from each part, so the inner operation is subtraction.

widget.prompt: Transfer to a final context: A group buys 9 passes at 25 dollars each and a voucher takes 11 dollars off. How many dollars?

commonErrors.feedback: That is the price before the voucher; the discount still has to come off.
A voucher reduces the bill, so the last step subtracts.

widget.prompt: A bar diagram shows 5 equal parts of 200 m, with 30 m crossed off inside each part. What does it record?

options.label: 5 × (200 − 30) = 850 m
options.feedback: Correct — the crossing sits inside every part, so each of the five parts is shortened by 30.

options.label: (5 × 200) − 30 = 970 m
options.feedback: That subtracts 30 only once, as if the mark sat at the end of the whole bar, not inside each part.

options.label: 5 + 200 − 30 = 175 m
options.feedback: Five equal 200-meter parts combine by multiplication, not by adding unlike quantities.

options.label: 5 × (200 + 30) = 1,150 m
options.feedback: Crossed off means removed from each part, so the inner operation is subtraction, not addition.
